title: Proof of Access: Archiving and Delegation Handbook
author: Ava Martinez
body:
SUMMARY
This handbook codifies a single, auditable approach to: (1) capturing authoritative proofs of access (authorization grants, delegation events, approval receipts), (2) long-term archiving of those proofs aligned to residency requirements, and (3) safe delegation workflows that integrate with incident response and the SDLC. It is intended for engineers, platform owners, SOC, and compliance reviewers.

GOALS AND SCOPE
- Ensure every privileged access event (human or machine) has a verifiable artifact stored in the audit index or the compliance archive.
- Standardize retention and custody rules by data residency and regulation band.
- Define delegation flows that minimize blast radius and are reversible.
- Provide clear steps for evidence packaging for regulatory requests or incident investigations.

OWNERSHIP AND ROLES
- Evidence Steward (primary): security-compliance@redwood.internal — responsible for retention policy enforcement and archive health.
- Service Owner: team owning the resource being accessed — responsible for tagging and attaching contextual metadata.
- Oncall SRE: operationalization of export and emergency access.
- Legal/Privacy: triage for cross-border requests and legal holds.

KEY PRINCIPLES
1) Source-of-truth: Authorization decisions must produce an immutable event to the audit stream before the request is granted.
2) Minimal delegation: Delegated tokens/roles must be timebound and scoped.
3) Provenance-first: Store contextual metadata (requestor, justification, approver, TTL, linked change-id) with each proof.
4) Defense-in-depth: Separate online audit index (fast search, 90d hot) from compliance archive (encrypted, geo-fenced long-term store).

RETENTION MATRIX (Summary)
| Evidence type | Hot index retention | Archive retention | Residency constraint | Encryption at rest | Owner |
|---------------|--------------------:|------------------:|---------------------|--------------------|-------|
| Privileged grant (console/portal) | 90 days | 7 years | Customer-region ; default US-EU split | AES-256 | Service Owner |
| Delegation token issuance | 30 days | 2 years | Same as resource | AES-256 | Security |
| Authorization decision logs (allow/deny) | 180 days | 7 years | Per-tenant residency | AES-256 with KMS per-region | SRE |
| Approval receipts (manual approvals) | 365 days | 7 years | Legal holds possible | AES-256 | Legal/Compliance |

Note: Specific regulatory buckets (e.g., financial, healthcare) may extend archive retention — consult Legal for final retention mapping.

PUSH AND ARCHIVE PATHS
- Live audit stream: kafka://audit-events (topic: authz-decisions, partitions keyed by tenant_id). Indexed in observability for quick queries (90d).
- Compliance archive: s3://compliance-archive/<region>/authz-proof/ (WORM-enabled buckets, server-side encryption with customer KMS for private deployments).

EVENT SCHEMA (canonical minimal fields)
- The canonical audit event is JSON. Example (trimmed):
{
  "event_id": "evt_01G9XYZ12345",
  "timestamp": "2026-02-14T18:12:22Z",
  "tenant_id": "tn-9a8b7",
  "actor": { "type": "user", "id": "alice@customer.com" },
  "action": "grant-role",
  "resource": "projects/finance-db",
  "role": "db-admin",
  "justification": "emergency fix",
  "approver": "bob@redwood.internal",
  "ttl_seconds": 3600,
  "proof_refs": ["approval-req-123", "change-456"]
}

PROCEDURE: Delegation issuance (engineer-facing)
1) Request flow: engineer creates a short-lived delegation request via redwoodctl or the Console. Must include: justification, linked change-id (if applicable), target scoping (resource path), and requested duration.
2) Approval flow: automatic approvals allowed only for pre-authorized runbooks. For ad-hoc requests, approval must be from an oncall or named approver for the service. Approval produces an approval_receipt event.
3) Token minting: upon approval, the token is minted with enforced TTL and recorded to the audit stream.
4) Post-issuance: the delegator must annotate related tickets and close with resolution. Expired tokens are automatically revoked and a revocation_event is written.

CLI examples
- Request: redwoodctl auth request-delegation --resource projects/infra --scope write --duration 1h --justification "migrate cert"
- Approve: redwoodctl auth approve --request-id approval-req-123 --approver bob@redwood.internal
- Export proof bundle (for compliance): redwoodctl audit export --tenant tn-9a8b7 --start 2026-01-01 --end 2026-01-31 --type grant,delegation --format tar.gz --output ./jan-proofs.tar.gz

EVIDENCE PACKAGING CHECKLIST (for regulators or legal)
- Include original event JSON(s) from audit stream.
- Include approval receipts and any human-readable rationale.
- Include associated change-ids and ticket links.
- Provide archival hash manifest (SHA-256) and signing metadata.
- State the region of origin and encryption keys used (KMS key IDs).

INCIDENT RESPONSE INTEGRATION
- When an incident references potential unauthorized access, Incident Commander requests an evidence pull from the compliance archive: runbook steps:
  1) Triage: confirm scope (tenant, resources, time window).
  2) Freeze: request a short-term lock on the affected archive partition (S3 object lock) to avoid overwrite or deletion.
  3) Snapshot: export the relevant audit events and approval receipts using redwoodctl audit export. Attach manifest and checksum to the incident ticket.
  4) Forensic review: Security + SRE analyze the event chain, entitlement binding, and any policy evaluation logs.
  5) Legal/Privacy: invoked if cross-border data or PII is involved.

SDLC GATE: How proof requirements map to release controls
- Pre-merge: any code that touches authorization logic must include unit tests that assert audit event emission.
- Staging: synthetic delegation flows must run in staging and documented in the test harness with a local archive sample.
- Release: release checklist includes a signed audit schema bump (if schema changes) and evidence regression test results.

RISK AND EXCEPTIONS PROCESS
- Exception requests (for retention truncation, cross-region archival changes, or unusual delegation lifetimes) must use the Risk Exceptions form and include: risk owner, compensating controls, rollback plan, and a sunset date.
- Exceptions are approved by the Risk Committee (security lead + legal + product). Approved exceptions are timebound and recorded in the central exceptions register.

METRICS AND MONITORING
- Archive health: daily job verifies object counts, checksum integrity, and KMS key access logs. SLA: < 1 missing object per 1M per month.
- Proof emission rate: alert if more than 0.1% of authorization decisions fail to produce an event.
- Tamper detection: periodic verify-signed-manifest job validates archival signatures; alert on signature drift.

AUDIT READINESS RUNBOOK (quick steps)
1) Identify required time window and tenants.
2) Run: redwoodctl audit export --tenant <id> --start <YYYY-MM-DD> --end <YYYY-MM-DD> --format tar.gz
3) Generate signature and manifest: sha256sum <file> > <file>.sha256; gpg --detach-sign <file>
4) Deliver bundle to Legal (use secure transfer; for high-sensitivity materials use customer KMS-wrapped archive).

APPENDICES
A. Example automated alert query (pseudo-SQL)
SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE event_type = 'grant-role' AND proof_refs IS NULL) / count(*) as missing_proof_rate FROM audit_events WHERE timestamp >= now() - interval '24h';

B. Example manifest format (text)
- manifest-version: 1
- created-by: redwood-evidence-exporter
- created-at: 2026-02-14T18:20:00Z
- items:
  - path: authz-proof/2026/02/14/evt_01G9XYZ12345.json
    sha256: <hex>
    region: us-west-2

C. Frequently asked questions
Q: How do we handle proofs for private deployments?
A: Private deployments must ship a managed export agent that mirrors approved proof bundles to the customer's KMS-wrapped archive endpoint. See the onprem packaging guide for details.

Q: What if an approver is unavailable for emergency access?
A: Use the emergency-runbook path with post-facto approval; emergency-grants are time-limited (max 4 hours) and require immediate creation of an incident ticket and approval_receipt post-hoc.
